source: Daily Investment Brief Macroeconomic Dashboard + authoritative-source supplementation
sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief remains the primary dashboard layer, but automated retrieval still exposes client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--'). No values are inferred from placeholders. MacroMicro remains supplemental where accessible. Current gaps are filled with official ISM/EIA/Federal Reserve data plus current Reuters market reporting. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard readings are inputs, not trading signals. Creator/video/social claims have zero direct score weight until independently verified.
regime: Refined-product inflation + elevated global long-end yields + softer hiring, while physical AI/industrial capex remains strong and time-to-power/microgrid demand is becoming more tangible. The result is a stagflationary quality split rather than a clean growth or recession regime.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Industrial expansion persists, but hiring and end-demand are cooling
channels.interpretation: August ISM Manufacturing remains expansionary at 54.6 with Production 58.3, but New Orders and Backlog cooled. ADP private payroll growth slowed to 38k and EIA total product supplied fell, so broad demand acceleration is no longer the base case.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: Oil inflation keeps hike risk elevated despite weaker hiring
channels.interpretation: September hike pricing moved around 70%. Weak ADP employment increases two-sided risk, but $90+ crude and extreme product cracks keep the Fed's inflation constraint active.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.interpretation: The US 10Y touched about 4.81% and closed near 4.78%, while the latest official 10Y real TIPS reference remains 2.44%. Long-duration, leveraged and pre-commercial equities still face a high discount-rate hurdle.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.interpretation: Quality issuers can still finance, but high risk-free rates and heavy infrastructure capital needs increase the premium on customer-funded projects and strong balance sheets.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: The last verified CCC-and-lower yield near 14.6% remains a dated stress marker rather than a live reading. High real yields and weaker hiring still point to unfavorable refinancing conditions for weak borrowers.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: High fuel/product prices, elevated borrowing costs and slower hiring pressure financed discretionary demand. Pawn/trade-down evidence supports persistent bifurcation, while EIA product supplied hints at early energy demand destruction.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: A 10Y around 4.8% keeps mortgage affordability and leveraged property activity under pressure; no fresh evidence justifies easing this channel.

channels.label: Industrial / Power Capex
channels.regime: Strong real bottlenecks; microgrid/time-to-power evidence strengthened
channels.interpretation: August ISM still shows electrical/component scarcity, while Vertiv's UtilityInnovation Group acquisition validates behind-the-meter generation, microgrid controls and specialised switchgear as commercial time-to-power bottlenecks. Continue filtering headline data-centre load requests for deposits and funding quality.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Energy, product, component and freight inflation extreme
channels.interpretation: ISM Prices stayed 71.1 and gasoline/diesel cracks remain extreme while copper, electrical/electronic components, memory, semiconductors, wire, fuel and freight are tight. Pricing-power suppliers benefit; low-margin users face a worsening squeeze.

channels.label: Labour
channels.interpretation: ADP private payrolls rose just 38k in August and ISM Manufacturing Employment slowed to 51.2. The signal is now softer, though official payrolls remain the next higher-authority test.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.interpretation: US equities rebounded Sep 2, but only after three losing sessions and with software still weak. The improvement is tactical; high yields, oil and weak hiring prevent a clean risk-on regime call.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent settled $95.63 and WTI $91.01 while EIA crude stocks fell 4.5M barrels. Physical tightness remains strong, but lower total product supplied is a warning that high prices are beginning to suppress demand.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: European gasoline cracks exceeded $62/bbl and diesel margins remained near $79/bbl over Brent. US refinery utilisation is already 98%, gasoline stocks fell and East Coast distillates remain exceptionally tight. Product scarcity is the strongest current energy-inflation channel.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: Global security premium with US feedgas advantage
channels.interpretation: European gas remains elevated as buyers seek secure supply. US LNG/take-or-pay infrastructure retains strategic value, while very high spot prices can still destroy price-sensitive demand.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Structural hedge intact; high real yields cap tactical upside
channels.interpretation: Gold rebounded near $4,368 as yields eased late in the session, but high real rates and a firm dollar still argue for staged exposure rather than momentum chasing.

themes.regime: Structural demand strong; microgrids/time-to-power strengthen while funded-load quality remains mandatory

watch.title: Behind-the-meter power and microgrids
watch.detail: VRT/UIG validates controls, switchgear and onsite-generation orchestration as real commercial bottlenecks.
watch.nextTest: VRT deal close, integration, backlog and hyperscaler microgrid deployments

watch.title: Ghost demand vs funded demand
watch.detail: Treat interconnection requests as provisional until deposits, ownership and funding are verified.

themes.regime: Physical demand real; time-to-power improving as investable subtheme while speculative request inflation remains exposed

watch.title: Funded projects
watch.detail: Prefer named customers, deposits, customer-funded capacity and booked supplier orders.

watch.title: Onsite power stack
watch.detail: Microgrid controls and behind-the-meter architecture can monetize before utility interconnections arrive.

themes.regime: Nitrogen scarcity strengthened but trade crowded

watch.title: Nitrogen advantage vs farmer affordability
watch.detail: CF benefits from low-cost North American gas versus disrupted global supply, but record-high equity pricing raises entry risk and farmer input demand remains elastic.
watch.nextTest: Urea/ammonia, Henry Hub, crop/input ratios, application rates

watch.title: Real yields and USD
watch.detail: Gold needs stabilization in real yields/USD before the tactical setup materially improves.
watch.nextTest: 10Y real yield, dollar and gold 200-day trend

watch.detail: Refinery utilisation is already near max while cracks remain extreme.
watch.nextTest: EIA inventories, cracks, refinery outages and product supplied

watch.detail: Americas crude and US LNG remain structural alternatives to Gulf dependence.

watch.title: High-rate pullbacks
